title: CuTe DSL Data Types for GPU Kernel Development
key_concepts: Native CuTe types map directly to hardware formats
Floating-point types include FP16, BF16, FP32, FP64, and new FP8
Integer types include Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64 and their unsigned counterparts
critical_patterns: Mixed-Precision GEMM: FP16 compute, FP32 accumulate
Dynamic Precision Selection: Compile-time flag for precision paths
constraints: FP16 has limited range and precision, suitable for deep learning
BF16 offers same range as FP32 but lower precision
FP8 is supported on Hopper+ for high performance
INT8 and INT4 are used for quantized operations with specific architectures
Type conversions must be explicit to avoid errors
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL provides a suite of data types optimized for GPU kernel development, crucial for leveraging tensor core operations, optimizing memory bandwidth, and ensuring numerical precision. The primary floating-point types include FP16, BF16, FP32, FP64, and the newer FP8 variants (E4M3 and E5M2) supported on Hopper and beyond. FP16 is widely used in deep learning due to its balance of performance and precision, while BF16 offers a broader range, making it suitable for large models. FP8 provides extreme performance gains on supported architectures. Integer types, including Int8 and Int4, are essential for quantized neural network operations, offering significant throughput improvements on compatible hardware. Mixed-precision patterns, such as computing in lower precision and accumulating in higher precision, are common in deep learning, enhancing both performance and accuracy. CuTe DSL supports explicit type conversions and follows standard type promotion rules, ensuring flexibility and precision in computations. Developers must consider architecture-specific optimizations, such as those available on Ampere and Hopper GPUs, to maximize performance. The decision tree for type selection emphasizes correctness, hardware compatibility, performance, and memory footprint. Debugging type issues often involves ensuring explicit conversions and matching accumulator types to operation precision. CuTe DSL's interoperability with frameworks like PyTorch is facilitated through type mapping and DLPack conversion, streamlining integration into existing workflows. Performance considerations highlight the importance of selecting the lowest precision that maintains accuracy, balancing memory bandwidth, compute throughput, and register usage. The document underscores the importance of aligning data types with hardware capabilities to achieve optimal GPU kernel performance.
